title: The Ground on Which a Carrier's Compensation Is Counted
content:
The money counted as compensation against a settled claim on the Travel Protection Plans is taken from the
carrier's ledger of the traveller's air bookings held under the Air Ticket Fare Brands, whose payout lines carry
both an amount and the ground the payout was raised on. Which of those grounds is counted depends on the head
the settlement the compensation answers was made on.

## The three readings

1. Where the settlement the compensation answers was made on a missed connection and the carrier's ledger
   carries payouts raised on an involuntary schedule change, the money counted is what the carrier has paid on
   that ground in those twelve months before the day the recovery is booked.
2. Where the settlement was made on a baggage head and the carrier's ledger carries payouts raised on an airline
   cancellation, the money counted is what the carrier has paid on that ground in those twelve months.
3. In every other case the money counted is the whole of what the carrier has paid out on the traveller's
   bookings in those twelve months, whatever ground each payout was raised on.

## The same three readings as a table

| Head the answered settlement was made on | What the carrier's ledger carries | The money counted |
|---|---|---|
| Missed connection | Payouts raised on an involuntary schedule change | What the carrier paid on that ground |
| A baggage head | Payouts raised on an airline cancellation | What the carrier paid on that ground |
| Any other combination | Whatever it carries | The whole of what the carrier paid out on the traveller's bookings |

Both parts of a reading must hold together. A settlement made on a missed connection where the carrier's ledger
carries no schedule-change payout at all falls to the third reading and counts the whole of the carrier's
payouts; so does a settlement made on a baggage head where the ledger carries no airline-cancellation payout.
